commands.name: install
commands.description: Install dependencies and reconcile the lockfile with package.json. NOT `npm ci`, and the difference is load-bearing: bootstrap prepares a tree that is being changed, so a turn that adds a dependency must be able to record it. `npm ci` refuses a lockfile that does not match, which made taking any dependency at all impossible through the belt. CI keeps `npm ci` — see .github/workflows/verify.yml — so the lockfile is still authoritative wherever the verdict counts (ADR 011). The lockfile diff is the sensor here; it does not block, and a change that grows it must be accounted for in the reason given.

commands.name: format
commands.description: Apply the repository's own formatting. Declared as bootstrap and ordered after install, because it runs prettier from node_modules and a tree that has not installed cannot format. It writes to the tree — that is the point, and it is why it is not a gate.

commands.name: build
commands.description: Emit dist/ from src/ using tsconfig.build.json. Bootstrap rather than gate for the same reason format is: it writes to the tree, and a gate whose verdict describes a tree it changed is not a verdict. Ordered after install because tsc comes from node_modules.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: The bar: typecheck, test, lint. One script, so the gate the belt runs and the gate CI runs cannot drift apart (S1).

commands.name: cli
commands.description: Start the emitted binary and check it refuses an empty diff. The only check in this repository that runs the artifact rather than the source, and the only one that can catch the emitted files landing somewhere bin does not point. Costs nothing: an empty diff returns before any client is constructed.

commands.name: review
commands.description: Run the review panel against the HEAD commit. A release step rather than a gate because it costs money — one model call per lens — and a gate that bills on every verification is a gate someone turns off. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment; without it the run reports which setting is missing and where to put it, and exits red without calling anything.

commands.name: diag-env-probe
commands.description: Temporary. No-cost probe: does CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN reach a spawned child, given an explicit env allow-list naming only that variable.

commands.name: diag-precompute-diff
commands.description: Temporary. Writes the fixed diff to a file, unrestricted (needs PATH to spawn git, which the OAuth-scoped step below cannot declare).

commands.name: diag-hypothesis
commands.description: Temporary. Arm A vs Arm B: broad-lens sampling vs narrow-lens splitting, on the OAuth path.

commands.name: make-corpus-diffs
commands.description: For every eval/corpus/<case> directory carrying a refs.json naming a real base/head branch, runs `git diff --merge-base origin/<base> origin/<head>` (scoped to refs.json's paths, when named) and writes the result to that case's own diff.txt. A case with no refs.json is left alone. Same reasoning and pattern as _diag-precompute-diff.mjs: no verb on the belt reports a diff, so this shells out to git directly, unrestricted, because it needs PATH to spawn git.

commands.name: eval-sweep
commands.description: Sweeps review fan width — how many lenses a panel is split into — against the practice corpus, at full and half corpus size, to find where recall, confirmed false positives and run-to-run stability trade off against cost, and whether the optimum moves with corpus size. Defaults to a dry run that calls no model and prints exactly what a real sweep would cost before anything is charged; `--spend` is required to actually spend, and every call across the whole sweep is capped at a shared concurrency limit (default 4) — the fix for the 429 storm `_diag-hypothesis` produced firing all its calls at once. A kept, committed, re-runnable measurement, not a diagnostic thrown away after use; see eval/README.md.

commands.name: eval-sweep-smoke
commands.description: SPENDS MONEY — a scoped smoke run of eval-sweep at --widths 1,3 only (72 calls), never the full default sweep. Exists because a declared release step's arguments are fixed at declaration time (nothing calling this step can pass extra argv through), so a first, deliberately small real run needs its own name rather than a flag on the everyday command. The general-purpose `eval-sweep` step stays argument-free and dry-run by default on purpose — a command that spends whenever anyone runs it is exactly the shape of thing that gets run by mistake. Run this once the transport is trusted at this scale; widen the swept axes only by editing this step's baked-in --widths or by running eval/sweep.mjs directly with --spend and explicit flags.

commands.name: eval-sweep-probe
commands.description: SPENDS A ROUNDING ERROR — exactly one real model call, made to answer "is the quota serving right now" before committing to a real spend. Run this before eval-sweep-smoke or eval-sweep-stage2 (or any real --spend run): a red result here means stop, the wall this harness's own first run hit for 49 minutes is still up, and no wider run will do anything but wait through the same wall for longer. A green result means the transport answered for real and a scoped real run is worth trying.

commands.name: eval-sweep-stage2
commands.description: SPENDS MONEY — the authorised stage 2 BRACKETING sweep: widths 8 and 21, full corpus only, default 3 repeats — 261 model calls (halved from 522 by dropping the half-corpus arm, which answers a scaling question this run is not asking). Each configuration comes back classified good/bad/indistinguishable per eval/criterion.mjs's stated rule, not ranked — a bracket ("10 good, 15 bad") is the goal, not a precise optimum. Run eval-sweep-probe first; do not run this if the probe came back red. Named for exactly what it spends on, same reasoning as eval-sweep-smoke: a declared release step's arguments are fixed at declaration time, so a scoped real run needs its own name rather than a flag on the argument-free, dry-run-by-default eval-sweep command that would otherwise get run by mistake. Aborts on its own after 20 consecutive HTTP 429 responses (MAX_CONSECUTIVE_429 in eval/sweep.mjs) rather than grinding through the whole sweep into a wall; a resulting partial results file can be finished later with --resume.
